an3.72:1.1: This monastery was favored by Ānanda, who was the teacher of Ghosita, the monastery’s donor ([sn35.129]()). He stayed there following the Buddha’s passing and the First Council ([sn22.90:4.2]()). Many, perhaps all, of the discourses featuring Ānanda here were set in the period after the Buddha’s death, including this one.
an3.72:1.2: For the Ājīvakas, see [an1.319:1.1](), [dn2:20.2](), and notes there.
an3.72:2.3: “Done well” (_sukata_) is not a standard term in this context. The Ājīvakas rejected the significance of kamma. It seems that this Ājīvaka householder, discontent with Ājīvaka teachings, was looking for something more satisfying.
